 :: J U D G M E N T :
:
The claim petition has been filed by the petitioner against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 03.05.2023.
2.

The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
That on 03.05.2023 at about 9.30 a.m., the petitioner was riding his Motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-50-W-2278 near Dibbur Koli Farm, Dibburu Village,
Hesaraghatta hobli, Yelahanka, Bengaluru District, at that time, the driver of Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-50-A-8593 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed SCCH-10 against the petitioner's Motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the injured petitioner was shifted to hospital and took inpatient treatment.
Further, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, he was working as a Security guard at Terrier Security Services India (pvt) Ltd., and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
On account of the injuries sustained in the accident, he could not do his work, he became permanently disabled and put to irreparable loss of income.
Further, the alleged accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle Tata Ace bearing Reg. No. KA-50-A- 8593.
The respondent No.1 being owner and the respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
the present petition.
3. In pursuance to the Petition notice, though the respondent No.1 has appeared before the Court through his SCCH-10 counsel, but not filed the written statement.
The respondent No.2 has appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement.

4. The brief contentions of the respondent No.2 (insurer) are as under:
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-50-A-8593 in the Shankar vs Gireesha.T on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102484659/
2 name of respondent No.1 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident,
however the liability if any subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further, denied the accident, the manner in which the accident took place, rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and its involvement in the alleged accident.
Further contended that, the petitioner has filed the false case against the offending vehicle for wrongful loss to this respondent.

Further, the respondent No.2 has denied the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident, treatment taken for those injuries, medical expenses SCCH-10 incurred and permanent disability suffered by him and also denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
On these grounds, respondent No.2 prayed for dismissal of the claim petition against it.
5. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-50-A-8593 by its driver,
in RTA took place on 03.05.2023 at about 9.30 a.m., near Dibbur Koli Farm, Dibburu Village, Hesaraghatta Hobli, Yelahanka, Bengaluru District ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what amount and from whom ?

3) What order or award?
6.
The petitioner, in order to prove his case examined himself as PW-1 and examined the doctor as PW-2 and in all SCCH-10 got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18.

The respondent No.2 has examined the doctor as RW-1 and also its official as RW-2 and in all got marked documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4.
7.
Heard the arguments.
Perused the materials available on record.

8. My findings to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order, for the following :
R E A S O N S 9.

ISSUE No.1:
Shankar vs Gireesha.

3
The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with respect to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 03.05.2023.
Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR No.0098/2023 of Rajamukunte PS and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, it reveal that I.O. has registered a case against the driver of the Tata Ace bearing Reg.
No.KA-50-A-8593 for the commission of SCCH-10 offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.7 is the copy of charge sheet filed by the Rajanukunte PS.

On perusal of Ex.P.7, it reveals that, after investigation the police have filed charge sheet against one Mr. Gireesha. T, who is none other than the respondent No.1/ driver cum owner of the offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No. KA-50-A- 8593 for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
10.
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 has seriously disputed the accident and also disputed the involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident.

According to the respondent No.2,
the offending vehicle was falsely implicated for the purpose of claiming compensation from the insurance company.
11. According to the petitioner, soon after the accident he was shifted to Government hospital Yelahanaka for first aid and later he was shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru for further treatment.
The respondent No.2 have examined the doctor of Yalahanka hospital as RW-1.
RW-1 has produced SCCH-10 the police intimation as Ex.R.1 and MLC extract as per Ex.R.2.
During the course of arguments, the learned counsel fore the respondent No.2 turned my attention towards Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.

On perusal of Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 it reveal that, in the said documents it is noted as under;
"History of self fall from bike (No. unknown) at 10.00 a.m. on 03.05.2023 near Rajanakunte Pass."
As per Ex.R.2 the patient was first seen at 10.30 a.m. on 03.05.2023.

Based on the above said note in the MLC register and police intimation, the counsel would submit that, the petitioner has sustained injury in a self fall and later the offending vehicle i.e. Tata Ace was falsely implicated for the purpose of claiming compensation.

In support of its contention the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has also relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2009 KAR 3562 in the case of Veerappa and another Vs Siddappa and another and ILR 2009 KAR 2921 in the SCCH-10 case of Bajaj Allianz Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs B.C. Kumar and another.

sentences.text: By relying on the aforesaid judgments, the counsel for the respondent No.2 would submit that, when the involvement of the offending vehicle itself is not proved, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation from the hands of the insurance company and the question of pleading guilty by the driver of the offending vehicle is not the sole criteria to allow the claim petition and hence, prayed to dismiss the petition filed against the insurance company.
12. I have once again gone through the documents produced by the petitioner.
Admittedly, after getting first aid from Yalahanka Government hospital, the petitioner/ injured was shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru for further treatment.
Ex.P.17 is the Case sheet issued by the Victoria hospital.

Shankar vs Gireesha.T on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102484659/
4

As per Ex.P.17, it reveals that the injured was admitted to the Victoria hospital on the same day i.e.
on 03.05.2023 at about 3.08 p.m.

In page No.5 of the Case sheet it is noted as under:
SCCH-10 "A/H/O RTA today morning 10:00 a.m, 2 wheeler v/s 4 wheeler near Rajankunte, patient sustained injury to face, left hand and left leg and chest."
13. There is no much time gap between the treatment given at Yalahanka Government hospital and the admission to the Victoria hospital.

Admittedly, when an accident occurs the person who is accompanying the patient to the hospital will be in a hurry to provide medical aid to the injured rather than to give complete information about the manner of accident.
Further, the person who is accompanying the injured to the hospital need not be an eyewitness.

In the instant case, though in Yalahanka Government hospital, the history of accident was given as self fall from the bike, but at the time of admission to the Victoria hospital on the same day within few hours, the history of accident was reported as 'RTA between 2 wheeler v/s 4 wheeler'.
Hence, I do not find any reason that, it is an after thought to implicate the offending vehicle in the accident to claim compensation.
SCCH-10 14. Ex.P.1 is the First Information Report.

Though it was registered on the next day of accident i.e.
on 04.05.2023, in the said FIR, the vehicle number of the offending vehicle was clearly mentioned.
It is also significant to note that, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle after investigation.
Hence, I do not find any reason of false implication of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident.

15. On perusal of the documents relied by the petitioner, it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and the petitioner has sustained injuries in the said accident.
16. Besides, it is settled principles of law that, in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

This view is supported by the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and SCCH-10 others Vs. Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.

sentences.text: 17. Thus, by considering the present facts of the case and the materials placed on record, I am of the opinion that, the accident in question had occurred due to the negligent and rash driving of the driver of the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-50-A-8593.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

18. ISSUE No.2:-

The petitioner contended that, after the accident, he was shifted to Government hospital, Yalahanka and after first aid for further treatment he was shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took inpatient treatment and spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses.

19. Before proceeding to discuss this issue, I feel it SCCH-10 necessary to reproduce the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2011(1) S.C.C page 343 in the case of Rajkumar Vs. Ajay Kumar.
In para No.5 of the judgment, Hon'ble Apex Court has mentioned the heads under which compensation is to be awarded in personal injury cases.
I reproduce the same hereunder for convenience.
Future Medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (general damages) SCCH-10 Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
Loss of amenities (and / or loss of prospects of marriage) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
Keeping in view the law declared in the aforementioned decision, I have carefully perused the entire materials placed on record.
The wound certificate of the petitioner has been marked as Ex.P.5.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained both simple and grievous injuries.
20. In this case, the petitioner has produced discharge card as per Ex.P.10.

On perusal of Ex.P.10 it reveals that, the petitioner was admitted to the Victoria hospital, Bengaluru on 03.05.2023 and discharged on 09.05.2023 and it also discloses that, the petitioner has sustained left sided closed distal 1/ 3rd end of radius fracture.
21.
Ex.P.11 are the medical bills amounting to Rs.16,063/- and Ex.P.12 are the medical prescriptions.
The medical bills SCCH-10 produced by the petitioner appears to be genuine.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for actual medical bills and same is rounded off to Rs.16,000/- under the head of Medical Shankar vs Gireesha.T on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102484659/
6 expenses.
22.

sentences.text: As per the medical documents it appear that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and he is suffering from physical disability.
By considering the nature of injury, the petitioner might have suffered pain and agony.
Considering the age of the petitioner, I am of the opinion that if Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards pain and sufferings it would be just.
If Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards nourishment and diet food it would be just.
23. The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury he has undergone surgery and suffering from permanent disability.
He has further stated that due to the disability he has lost his earning capacity.

In order to establish the disability, the doctor was examined before the Court as PW- 2. PW-2 during his evidence has deposed that, the petitioner SCCH-10 has sustained Left closed distal 1/3rd of radius fracture and took treatment of internal fixation of radius and regular follow up treatment in Victoria hospital.

Further deposed that, recently for assessment of disability, he examined the petitioner on 12.02.2024 and on examination it is found that the petitioner has restriction of joint movement of left wrist palmar and fracture is united and implant in situ.

Further,
the petitioner has suffered physical impairment disability of 29% to left upper limb and 10% to the whole body.

Though PW-2 doctor was cross-examined by the counsel for the respondent No.2,
nothing was elicited from the mouth of the witness to disprove his evidence.
24. According to the petitioner, he was aged about 38 years at the time of accident and was working as Security guard at Terrier Security Services India (pvt) Ltd., and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/-
p.m. In order to prove his avocation and income, the petitioner has produced the copy of the ID card issued by the Terrier Security Service and Bank account SCCH-10 statement.
Though the petitioner has produced the said bank account statement it does not reveal the actual salary drawn by the petitioner as security guard.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2023(4) KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another.

entities.text: Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above decision the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru (KSLSA in short).

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The KSLSA, Bengaluru as per letter dated 26.02.2022 - 01/NLA/2022/550/2022 has circulated the notional income chart prepared by them.
As per the said notional income chart, the income for the year 2022 is fixed as Rs.15,500/-

Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court and the letter of KSLSA and also in the absence of proof of income, this Court is of the opinion that, if the notional income is taken into consideration for assessing the income of the petitioner would be just and SCCH-10 proper.
The accident was occurred on 03.05.2023.
Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.16,000/- as monthly income of the petitioner.
25. On perusal of the medical documents and medical evidence it is crystal clear that, the petitioner cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier.
Hence, the disability of the petitioner will definitely come in the way of the petitioner in his future earnings.

sentences.text: As per the doctor, the whole body disability is approximately 10%.
It is settled principles that all permanent disabilities arising out of injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity
. The percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability.

Even though the doctor has opined 10% permanent disability to the whole body, considering the nature of work of the petitioner and considering the disability, I assess the petitioner's loss of future earning capacity as 9%.
SCCH-10 27.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the Driving licence as per Ex.P.8.

As per Ex.P.8,
the date of birth of petitioner is shown as 10.06.1983.
The accident was occurred on 03.05.2023.
Hence, the age of the petitioner is considered as 40 years at the time of accident and multiplier applicable for his age is 15.
The loss of future earning capacity is assessed as 9%.
The annual income is assessed Rs.1,92,000/-(Rs.16,000 x 12).
Therefore, the loss of future income would be Rs.1,92,000/-(annual income) X 15 (multiplier) X 9% = Rs.2,59,200/-.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future income of Rs.2,59,200/-.
28.
The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury and disability he is unable to do any physical strain works and the disability is coming in the way of his day today activities and avocation.
Hence, considering the injuries suffered, this Court is of the opinion that, due to disability, the petitioner must forego some comforts in his life.
Hence, I SCCH-10 conclude that if Rs.25,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities it would be just.
29. PW-2 doctor in his evidence has stated that, the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants.
Admittedly, the petitioner has not produced any estimation for removal of implants.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, if Rs.20,000/- is awarded towards future medical expenses it will be just and this amount shall not carry any future interest.

30. Thus, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads;
Sl.
 Heads Compensation No.
1) Medical expenses Rs. 16,000 /-
2) Pain and sufferings Rs. 30,000/-
3) Nourishment and diet food Rs. 10,000 /-
 Loss of Future earning Rs. 2,59,200/-
4) capacity due to permanent  disability 5) Loss of amenities Rs. 25,000 /-
6) Future Medical expenses Rs. 20,000/-
 SCCH-10  Total Rs.3,60,200/-

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,60,200/-.
31. REGARDING LIABILITY:
As discussed supra, this Court has arrived at the conclusion that, the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-50-A-8593.
In this case, the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 has insured the vehicle with respondent No.2, as such, respondent No.2 has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Admittedly, the Insurance Policy was in force at the time of the accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the respondent No.1 RC owner of the vehicle and respondent No.2 insurer are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award.

The respondent No.2 being insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation of Rs.3,60,200/- along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
SCCH-10
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
32. Issue No.3:

In view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,60,200/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.2 being insurer is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Out of the award amount, 25% of the award amount shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 2 years in any nationalized bank of petitioner's choice and balance amount shall be released in favour SCCH-10 of the petitioner through NEFT / RTGS by way of E- payment on proper identification.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.

It is settled principles that all permanent disabilities arising out of injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity
. The percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability.
Even though the doctor has opined 10% permanent disability to the whole body, considering the nature of work of the petitioner and considering the disability, I assess the petitioner's loss of future earning capacity as 9%.
SCCH-10 27.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the Driving licence as per Ex.P.8.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future income of Rs.2,59,200/-.
28.
The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury and disability he is unable to do any physical strain works and the disability is coming in the way of his day today activities and avocation.
Hence, considering the injuries suffered, this Court is of the opinion that, due to disability, the petitioner must forego some comforts in his life.
The respondent No.1 has insured the vehicle with respondent No.2, as such, respondent No.2 has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Admittedly, the Insurance Policy was in force at the time of the accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the respondent No.1 RC owner of the vehicle and respondent No.2 insurer are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award.

The respondent No.2 being insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation of Rs.3,60,200/- along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
32. Issue No.3:
In view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,60,200/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.2 being insurer is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Out of the award amount, 25% of the award amount shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 2 years in any nationalized bank of petitioner's choice and balance amount shall be released in favour SCCH-10 of the petitioner through NEFT / RTGS by way of E- payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.
